rules.pattern: Overlap-friendly double buffering of in-flight tiles
rules.rule: Allocate separate receive buffers distinct from the home tile and select source via a compile-time-style pointer swap (own tile when you are the broadcaster, buffer otherwise) — this lets the next broadcast land without corrupting the operand currently being consumed.

rules.pattern: DSD-based rank-1 update inner kernel
rules.rule: Express the local tile update as an outer loop over the shared K dimension issuing @fmacs on a mem1d_dsd that walks a full column of A scaled by one scalar of B, and stride the C DSD across N — one DSD issue replaces an inner scalar k-loop and uses the FMAC unit at peak.

rules.pattern: Column-major tile layout aligned to the SIMD/DSD axis
rules.rule: Store local A/B/C tiles column-major so the contiguous DSD stride matches the vectorized accumulation direction; mismatched layout forces gather-style addressing and kills DSD throughput.

rules.pattern: Persistent kernel with step counter and self-reactivation
rules.rule: Implement the P-step loop as a persistent task that increments a step variable and re-invokes the communication phase from within the compute completion handler, rather than relaunching a kernel per step — eliminates host round-trips and lets the fabric pipeline stay primed.

rules.pattern: Comptime-specialized tile dimensions
rules.rule: Pass per-PE tile extents (Mt, Kt, Nt) as comptime params so DSD descriptors, loop bounds, and buffer sizes are resolved at compile time; this removes runtime address arithmetic from the hot loop and enables the compiler to fuse DSD setup.

rules.pattern: Edge-PE scatter + axis broadcast for operand distribution
rules.rule: Seed full input vectors on a single edge PE, scatter them along one axis of the grid, then broadcast orthogonally down the other axis — this exploits fabric routers for O(log) or pipelined distribution instead of having every PE fetch from global memory like a GPU would.

rules.pattern: DSD-driven outer loop over the contraction dim
rules.rule: Express the local matrix-times-vector as a loop over the short dimension issuing a single strided-DSD @fmacs per step (column of A times scalar of x into the full output vector) — one instruction streams an entire column, removing per-element loop overhead and feeding the FPU at peak rate.

rules.pattern: Fuse bias into the local compute on the owning PE
rules.rule: Add the bias/elementwise term inside the compute task on whichever PE column already owns it, before the cross-PE reduction — this avoids a separate post-reduction kernel launch and an extra pass over the output, and costs nothing because the reduction identity preserves the added value.

rules.pattern: Home-tile vs receive-buffer aliasing
rules.rule: Allocate a persistent 'home' tile plus a separate receive buffer per operand, and at each step pick the pointer based on whether this PE is the broadcast source; this lets the broadcasting PE skip a self-copy and lets receivers double-buffer in-flight data without clobbering their own home tile.

rules.pattern: DSD-based rank-1 update inner kernel
rules.rule: Express the per-step local GEMM as an outer loop over the contraction index issuing @fmacs on a mem1d_dsd column of C with a scalar from B and a strided DSD over A; one DSD issue streams a whole column, eliminating per-element address arithmetic and the inner scalar k-loop a naive port writes.

rules.pattern: Column-major tile layout matched to the FMAC stride
rules.rule: Store local A and C tiles column-major so that the rank-1 update's contiguous DSD walks unit-stride memory while the scalar broadcast comes from B; matching tile layout to the DSD access pattern keeps the FMAC pipeline fed at one element/cycle instead of incurring strided gather penalties.

rules.pattern: Comptime tile dimensions and resource binding
rules.rule: Pass per-PE tile extents, queue IDs, and DSR IDs as comptime params so DSD shapes, broadcast lengths, and loop trip counts are fixed at compile time; this hoists all address math out of the steady state and lets the compiler statically allocate fabric resources, which a runtime-shaped naive kernel cannot do.

rules.pattern: Self-reentrant step loop instead of host relaunch
rules.rule: Have the compute task increment the SUMMA step counter and tail-call the broadcast entry until P steps complete, then activate an exit task; keeping the iteration on-device avoids host round-trips per step that would otherwise dominate at wafer scale.

rules.pattern: DSD-strided MAC over scalar inner loop
rules.rule: Express the per-column rank-1 update as a strided mem1d_dsd over the output accumulator combined with a fused multiply-add using the scalar x element as the operand — a single DSD issue streams the whole column of A into the accumulator, removing per-element loop overhead and index arithmetic that a scalar k-loop incurs.

rules.pattern: Comptime-bind tile shapes and topology
rules.rule: Pass tile dimensions and the PE rectangle extents as comptime params so DSDs, loop trip counts, and collective participant counts are all resolved at compile time — this removes runtime bounds checks (the (N+TILE-1)/TILE and if(col<N) guards a naive kernel needs) and lets the compiler fully unroll/pipeline the inner update.

rules.pattern: Keep scalars on-fabric to avoid D2H sync
rules.rule: After a reduction, immediately consume the scalar (invert, multiply, compare) on the PE that produced it instead of shipping it to the host and back; host-mediated scalars force a global barrier and destroy pipelining of successive iterations.

rules.pattern: Replace scalar accumulation loops with DSD/BLAS-style bulk ops
rules.rule: Express vector updates like x = y * s or ||y||^2 using strided DSD descriptors or a vendor BLAS micro-library so the operation issues as one streaming instruction over the whole local segment — removes per-element loop overhead and lets the compiler bind dedicated DSRs.

rules.pattern: Keep all solver state PE-resident
rules.rule: Allocate x, r, p, w, and scratch scalars in PE-local memory for the entire solve and only memcpy at setup/teardown; avoiding per-iteration host staging is what makes the per-iteration cost scale with fabric latency rather than IO bandwidth.

rules.pattern: Distribute matrix as physical stencil, not dense GEMV
rules.rule: For SpMV in iterative solvers where the operator is a structured stencil, map the unknown grid onto the PE fabric and exchange only halo faces via a stencil module instead of replicating a dense matrix and doing per-row reductions — communication cost drops from O(N) all-to-all per row to O(surface) nearest-neighbor per step.

rules.pattern: Comptime-bound vector lengths and DSD shapes
rules.rule: Hoist per-PE tensor lengths, block sizes, and DSD descriptors to comptime/params and bind them once at init, so inner-loop ops carry no runtime shape checks or address arithmetic — the naive translator recomputes bounds every kernel call.
